result.summary: Independently re-verified REQ-418. (1) TEST_PARALLEL_N=4 scripts/test_parallel.sh, run alone: 'combined: 4999 tests, 6 properties, 6 failures (4999/5005 passed)'. Attributed each failure structurally via `git diff main --stat` on the failing file and its source: Letflow.Docs.RequirementStatusInvariantsTest (docs-drift class, test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs -- zero diff vs main), Mix.Tasks.Letflow.CheckBoundariesTaskTest AC2 (ISS-0832-class MIX_TEST_PARTITION/MIX_ENV=dev subprocess flake -- zero diff vs main on that test file or lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_boundaries*.ex), Letflow.RouterTest x2 (ISS-0827-class stale deferred-route-count guard -- zero diff vs main on test/letflow/router_test.exs or lib/letflow/router.ex), Letflow.IdentityTest x2 (ISS-0766-class bpm-default tenant displacement flake via test/support/bpm_default_realm_displacement.ex -- zero diff vs main on test/letflow/identity_test.exs or lib/letflow/identity.ex). None of REQ-418's changed files (mobile_tenant_config.ex, bpm-default.json, the new/edited test files) appear anywhere in this failure set -- all 6 are pre-existing and unrelated. (2) Also independently ran `mix letflow.check.test` (the stricter ISS-0069 gate) three times to get a clean read: first at default N=16 (nproc) was killed early as noise; a second TEST_PARALLEL_N=4 run overlapped briefly with the killed run and surfaced 4 extra Letflow.ServiceCatalogReaperTest failures that are ISS-0414's own concurrent-invocation guard correctly detecting my own overlapping mix test process (self-inflicted contamination, discarded); a third, single, clean TEST_PARALLEL_N=4 run reproduced exactly the same 6 pre-existing failures/files as (1) above (`Result: 1227/1229 passed ... Failed: 2 tests` for the last-dumped partition; full dump: RequirementStatusInvariantsTest x1, IdentityTest x2, CheckBoundariesTaskTest x1, RouterTest x2 = 6 total), exited 1 only for that reason -- zero occurrences of the ISS-0069 target substring 'default values for the optional arguments' anywhere in that run's captured output (grep -c = 0). (3) Ran the three REQ-418 test files directly (keycloak_realm_mobile_client_test.exs, mobile_tenant_config_test.exs, tenant_config_test.exs): 47 passed. (4) Re-ran `mix test --include keycloak test/letflow/integration/keycloak_mobile_client_auth_test.exs` against the live letflow-keycloak-1 container (confirmed healthy via `docker ps`, still carrying TEST-RUNNER's force-recreated realm import -- did not force-recreate again since the test passed against the existing container state): 4 passed (AC3a/b/c, AC4). (5) Re-checked all 8 acceptance criteria directly against code: AC1/AC2 -- read priv/keycloak/realms/bpm-default.json's diff vs main: letflow-mobile appended as a new clients[] element with the exact publicClient/standardFlowEnabled/directAccessGrantsEnabled:false/implicitFlowEnabled:false/pkce.code.challenge.method:S256/redirectUris (exact one-element list, no '*'/http)/webOrigins:[]/roles-mapper/oidc-audience-mapper(included.client.audience:letflow-web, access.token.claim:true) shape; letflow-web's object is untouched (diff shows only an addition, no modification hunk). AC3/AC4 -- live keycloak_mobile_client_auth_test.exs run, 4/4 passing against the real container. AC5/AC6 -- read lib/letflow/routers/mobile_tenant_config.ex directly: mobile_config_map/2 returns the six keys realm_url/locales/default_locale/branding/environment_kind/client_id; client_id/0 resolves System.get_env("MOBILE_OIDC_CLIENT_ID") || "letflow-mobile"; test file's @expected_keys and dedicated client_id-value/env-override/cross-path-identity tests are present and passing (47/47 above). AC7 -- read the moduledoc directly: 'exactly five keys' does not appear anywhere in the file (grep-equivalent visual scan of the full moduledoc); it now states 'It returns exactly six keys: realm_url, locales, default_locale, branding, environment_kind, client_id' and the full three-point client_id reasoning (public-client id is not a secret / RFC 6749 §2.2; platform-global, byte-identical across every never-error branch; server-sent avoids app-release coupling), plus 'Adding a seventh key to this response is a security change, not a feature' (correctly renumbered forward). Also confirmed the cross-module test/letflow/routers/tenant_config_test.exs AC7 guard was correctly updated from asserting 'exactly five keys' to 'exactly six keys' (a legitimate, REQ-418-caused update to a different requirement's regression test, not scope creep). AC8 -- SECURITY-REVIEWER's step-02c-security-reviewer.json result.status is PASS (confirmed by direct read); mix letflow.check.test's real output is quoted above (fails only on the 6 pre-existing, structurally-unrelated failures, not on anything REQ-418 touched, and not on the ISS-0069 substring). (6) docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-418 entry is still status: pending as expected (DOC-UPDATER's job next); docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml has no REQ-418 entry yet, also expected pending DOC-UPDATER. No other staleness found. VERDICT: PASS.
